resources.note: Claude Code has no separate information channel: resources arrive as prompt text or as files the agent reads, and their lower authority rests on framing only.

model.name.note: Maps to --model or the model setting; accepts an alias or a full model name.

model.effort.note: Maps to --effort; available levels depend on the model, and an unsupported level falls back to the highest supported level below it.

skills.note: Maps to SKILL.md skills under .claude/skills; Skill(name) permission rules limit which skills the agent may load.

mcpServers.note: Maps to --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config; stdio and HTTP transports are supported.

plan.note: Maps to TaskCreate/TaskUpdate, or to TodoWrite; each update appears as a tool_use block in the message stream. The tools are offered by default only on some models, so the host sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1.

planFirst.auto.note: Maps to plan mode. The host keeps plan mode's lock by giving no allow rules during it, so every call that is not read-only reaches its canUseTool callback, and by setting useAutoModeDuringPlan to false in local settings so the auto mode classifier approves no command while planning; plan mode keeps its blocks in Agent SDK sessions. A PreToolUse hook on ExitPlanMode returns allow with updatedInput, so the plan is accepted at once, then the host calls setPermissionMode.

planFirst.ask.note: Maps to plan mode. The host keeps plan mode's lock by giving no allow rules during it, so every call that is not read-only reaches its canUseTool callback, and by setting useAutoModeDuringPlan to false in local settings so the auto mode classifier approves no command while planning; plan mode keeps its blocks in Agent SDK sessions. A PreToolUse hook on ExitPlanMode receives the plan; the host asks for approval, allows it with updatedInput, or denies it with the comment as the reason Claude sees, and after approval calls setPermissionMode.

instance.new.note: Each claude -p or Agent SDK query without --resume or --continue starts a new session; --no-session-persistence discards it.

delivery.steer.note: Agent SDK streaming input: a user message sent during a turn, with default priority, is read in the same turn once the running tool calls finish.

reviewer.person.note: In the default permission mode, ask rules prompt the user, or the host through canUseTool.

reviewer.model.note: Maps to the auto permission mode: a classifier judges actions that no rule decides, so an AgSDL ask is exported without an ask rule, which would still prompt a person. The classifier also judges some actions the document allows, since broad allow rules are set aside, and it falls back to manual approvals after repeated blocks.

directories.note: Maps to additionalDirectories for the file tools, and to sandbox allowWrite for writable directories. Added directories are writable by sandboxed commands and editable by the file tools, so read directories also get Edit deny rules, merged into denyWrite.

read.note: Read rules govern the file tools and recognized Bash file commands; Read deny paths are merged into the sandbox denyRead list, which covers every Bash subprocess when sandbox.enabled, sandbox.failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands false are set (macOS and Linux only); ask paths also go to denyRead so that only the Read tool, which asks, can reach them. sandbox.excludedCommands stays empty. Reads outside the zone: permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories makes the file tools refuse them, and denyRead with allowRead for the zone covers Bash.

write.note: The sandbox limits Bash writes to the working directory and Edit allow paths, Edit deny paths are merged into denyWrite, and Edit rules govern the file tools; ask paths also go to denyWrite so that only the Edit tool, which asks, can write them; requires the sandbox settings listed under read.

shell.note: Bash(pattern) rules match the command text, including each subcommand of a compound command, but not programs that a matched command starts; a bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands unless sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed is false.

network.note: The sandbox proxy refuses Bash connections to hosts outside allowedDomains or in deniedDomains, WebFetch(domain:...) rules govern WebFetch, and WebSearch must be denied unless network is fully allowed; ask hosts go to deniedDomains so that only WebFetch, which asks, can reach them; requires the sandbox settings listed under read. Hosts outside the allowlist are denied rather than prompted only with sandbox.network.strictAllowlist true, read from user or managed settings. Monitor must be denied unless network is fully allowed: its WebSocket source is limited by deniedDomains, not by allowedDomains.

mcp.note: mcp__server and mcp__server__tool rules; MCP servers themselves run outside the sandbox.

delegate.note: Agent rules (formerly Task) and Workflow rules govern subagents, which inherit the parent's permission rules and its deny and ask rules in every mode; subagent definitions must not set permissionMode, which applies when the parent runs in default or dontAsk mode and can allow calls the parent would deny.

outputStyle.description: Name of an output style, case-sensitive, for example Explanatory, Learning, Concise or Proactive, or a custom style. Applies to the main conversation only.

alwaysThinkingEnabled.description: Settings key alwaysThinkingEnabled; false turns extended thinking off. No effect on models that always think, such as Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable.

maxTurns.description: Maps to --max-turns: the number of agentic turns after which a print-mode run exits with an error.
